title: Securing Session Persistence in Financial Portals
business: Financial service providers managing authenticated user sessions for retail banking applications.
problem: Session hijacking via Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) and unauthorized client-side script access to sensitive session tokens stored in browser cookies.
solution: Implementing defense-in-depth via cookie attributes that restrict token exposure to network-only transit and prevent cross-site context leakage.
steps: Set the HttpOnly flag to prevent JavaScript access to the session cookie.
Apply the Secure flag to ensure cookies are only transmitted over encrypted HTTPS connections.
Configure the SameSite attribute to Strict or Lax to mitigate cross-site request forgery risks.
Define a narrow scope using the Path and Domain attributes to limit cookie visibility to specific application endpoints.
outcome: Reduced risk of session token theft and unauthorized cross-site actions, ensuring session integrity remains within the intended application boundary.
limitation: Strict SameSite configurations may break legitimate cross-site authentication flows, such as OAuth redirects; verify functionality by testing session persistence across third-party identity provider callbacks.

diagram.title: Cookie Security Enforcement Flow
diagram.description: The flow shows how the server enforces security attributes during the Set-Cookie response to the browser.

code.content: res.cookie('session_id', 'xyz123', { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'Strict' }); // Enforces browser-level protection
code.explanation: This code maps to the solution by setting the HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes on the session cookie to prevent client-side script access and cross-site leakage.
